Grateful to have been IN THE ROOM with Ivan Galanin, Founder of @adipeau at the stunning @livingbeauty.shop for an intimate lunch alongside an inspiring group of women.

We learned all about the Adipeau product line and how the Strength Gel and Cream can actually help improve the appearance of skin that has weakened, changed and lost volume over time. The results Ivan shared that customers have had were pretty incredible and as a girl who does mostly natural skincare and simple facials, I can’t wait to try them!

My favourite moment was when Ivan shared that taking care of the mind is the best way to take care of your skin. If you’re mentally healthy, you make better food choices, you feel more rested, you’re not overthinking and therefore, you’re putting less stress on your body and skin.

So simple, but SO true.

I always leaving these rooms with fresh perspectives, meaningful conversations, and new connections. Thanks for having me @adipeau @livingbeauty.shop

At the start of this year I told myself I wanted to have more fun with my work. When I closed my community events business after 8 years, I started to explore my creativity more and also looked back on things I did in the past that would light me up.

When I was a teenager I worked as an extra for movies and TV shows, and I also did some modelling for various magazines. I loved being on set, even with the long hours!

Over the years I only kept up with it when brands would reach out to me or people would ask if I’d participate in campaigns, but at the beginning of this year I thought “what if I started to explore this a little more”?

A few months ago I came across a casting call through an agency and something told me to apply. Well I landed the campaign immediately, and turns out, it was for a brand I love (@shophealthhut) and a founder I know (Hi, Tara 👋🏼)! 

I had the best time shooting this for the launch of @shophealthhut’s new product line. It was such a great reminder that we can honestly do anything we love at ANY age. 

And why should we tell ourselves otherwise?

We owe it to ourselves to pursue our curiosities instead of thinking we’re too late. 

p.s. go check out the new line of Health Hut products, I can attest to the fact that they are incredible!

caption:
BTS of IN THE ROOM with @itsconnielo and @laura.athompson co-founders of @threeshipsbeauty. (plus a look at 9 years of shared history…swipe for the photos)! 👀 

In 2017 I was building my own business through community events in Toronto. Around that same time, Connie and Laura were starting to build Three Ships Beauty (then Niu Body!).

We were introduced when they started sampling their products at events I was hosting, and what began as a collaboration quickly turned into a friendship. Over the years, I’d visit their pop-ups, model for photoshoots, host events with them, partner on giveaways, and have the privilege of watching their dream grow into a multi-million-dollar company and one of Canada’s leading skincare brands. 

Connie and Laura are two of the hardest-working people I know. They lead with integrity, care deeply about what they create, and I’m so proud to call them my friends.

That’s why filming this episode of IN THE ROOM felt so special.

Yes, we talk about entrepreneurship — being on @cbcdragon, Forbes 30 Under 30, and what it takes to build a successful company. But we also talk about their desire of becoming moms while building a business, Laura’s brain tumour diagnosis, the support of their husbands, friendship, health, purpose, and even slowing down to make matcha together. 🍵 

One of my favourite parts of hosting IN THE ROOM is creating space for conversations that move beyond someone’s résumé. Because behind every successful company are real people navigating work, relationships, health, and life—just like the rest of us.

Congratulations, Connie and Laura. I’m so proud of everything you’ve built—and even more proud of the women you’ve become along the way. 🤍

EPISODE 5 of IN THE ROOM with @itsconnielo and @laura.athompson, the incredible co-founders of @threeshipsbeauty , is out now. ✨🧴

I had the opportunity to sit down with Connie and Laura for a conversation that went far beyond entrepreneurship. Having known them for 8+ years, it was especially meaningful to share not only the story of the business they’ve built, but also the women behind it.

We talked about how they first bonded over their shared frustration with expensive, ineffective “natural” skincare and turned just $4,000 into a nationally recognized beauty brand. Along the way, we discuss the realities of building a multi-million-dollar company, from appearing on Dragon’s Den to being recognized on Forbes 30 Under 30.

But what makes this conversation so special is everything beyond the business. We talk about the desire to build families while building a company, the support of their partners, Laura’s brain tumour diagnosis and the perspective it brought, the importance of friendship, and creating a life that feels as meaningful as the work itself. We even step into the kitchen to make matcha together! 

This episode is a reminder that behind every successful company are people navigating life’s biggest questions with courage, vulnerability, and purpose.

If you’ve ever dreamed of building something of your own, are curious about the stories behind successful founders, or simply enjoy thoughtful conversations about work and life, I hope you’ll join us.

I had the chance to share a pizza making experience, lunch and intimate conversation at home with Philip Lago and Mystique Mattai, the husband-and-wife duo behind @chef.souschef. Of course we chatted a lot about food, but also about having a family, traveling with toddlers and the joy of bringing people together.

We talked about how turning their post-wedding blues into a food blog just three days after getting married unexpectedly changed the course of their lives, growing into a beloved online community, a published cookbook, and so much more!!

If you’ve ever believed that some of life’s best moments happen around the dinner table (even with little ones!), dreamed of building something with the person you love, or simply want a reminder to slow down and savour the everyday, this episode is for you.

It was a pleasure to spend the day inside Mystique and Phil’s kitchen and inside their gorgeous home. Making pizza from scratch, chatting about their love story and growing their family (they have 3 kids under the age of 5), and what’s next for them over a delicious lunch. 

This was a day where I was truly “in the room”, getting to share a piece of their everyday lives with them.

caption:
For my sweet 16 I co-hosted a huge birthday party with my friend Ashley (also a Sagittarius!), and we pretty much invited the entire grade....except there was a MASSIVE snowstorm and other than my sister and her best friend who’s condo party room we were hosting in, a total of 5 people were actually able to get out of the house and show up. We were left with 10 party sized pizzas and a night of taking decor down. 😢 Not the way you want to remember a 16th birthday.

I’ve always loved birthdays and loved the idea of bringing people together to celebrate whether it was mine or anyone else’s, but every year as my birthday nears I have mixed feelings about it, likely from some of those experiences in my younger years. My mom told me that every year I’d plan my own parties months in advance, but I remember on the day of, I’d also have moments of disappointment.

All that to say, this year was a lot of the same feelings, except that when I look back a week later I can reflect on how many beautiful moments and meals were shared with family and friends, the outpouring of love that I felt from people near and far, and the incredible experiences I got to have including a bunch of surprises along the way. In retrospect...I’m so grateful for all of it.

So this is just a message to say that if you too don’t feel like your bday is what you hoped for it to be, or that something isn’t matching your expectations, or maybe you just feel a little sad...that’s OK. Just find the moments that you can feel grateful for and then life will bring you more of those as the years go by. 🤎 

Thank you to everyone that made this one special—I love you and I’m lucky to have you!

caption:
It’s hard to sum up an entire month away in one tiny grid post when there are so many experiences, reflections, beautiful moments and things that can change you. So I’m breaking it down.

First up from my trip was Singapore where we spent 3 nights, staying at @thestandard.singapore. This was my 2nd time visiting, but this time the weather was sunnier which allowed us to venture out and explore a little more.

I was in AWE of how clean, organized and efficient the city is. It felt like it’s wasn’t even real!

From the spotless sidewalks, to parks and lush greenery everywhere (literally, hanging off many buildings), to the extremely on-time transit system, this is a city that I felt SO content and safe in.

It’s extremely liveable, and based on my conversations with friends and cousins that live there, Singapore does an amazing job in investing in the future of its residents. They are already making plans for developmental projects in 2050 which is incredible. 

While walking the streets, I couldn’t help but envy many of the things I wish that Toronto would have more of.

Overall I LOVED the food (I could eat noodles every day), the cleanliness, the design of the buildings and green spaces, the ability to take public transit EVERYWHERE, the innovation, the airport (and the newly built @jewelchangiairport), the hotels, the monkeys (!), the overall peace and quiet, the shopping, and the elevated/luxurious vibe.

What I didn’t love was the amount of people I saw on transit glued to their phones. We were literally the only ones on every subway ride we took that weren’t buried in our screens, watching endless videos (I could see how fast people were scrolling, or switching between videos). It was actually quite alarming to have a completely silent train ride, but with ZERO eye contact with other humans.

I think it’s partly because it’s super organized city of residents that respect rules and so everything feels peaceful YET on the other hand it tends to create more of a quiet, inward culture where it’s the norm to keep to yourself. 

Have you been to Singapore? Would love to hear your thoughts!👇🏼

caption:
Camera roll from Bali (the 2nd stop of our month away!) — Pt. 1

Indonesia was actually the 40th country I’ve traveled to, in my 40th year of life. 

It’s been on my list for a long time, and as the years went by I kept hearing more and more about how touristy it has become, how it’s changed, how it’s full of digital nomads.

But in my experience, Bali is still the beautiful Bali that people know and love...you just have to find the magic. 

We decided to stay at the GORGEOUS @mundukcabins, about 3 hour drive up north from the airport, because it came recommended by two friends who have impeccable taste and have both spent long periods of time in Bali (thank you @meganheddinger and @carmenntsangdiego, you were sooo right 🫶🏽). I wanted to gatekeep this because it’s honestly that special. 

There are only 6 private cabins on the property, and for 3 days we barely saw anyone else except for the staff who made our experience so incredible from the fresh breakfast in our room, afternoon tea, in-room massages, happy hour by the infinity pool and more. 

We were fully immersed in nature, and despite not wanting to leave our stunning room, we ventured out for a day trip to some waterfalls, the stunning rice fields, a coffee tour and visits to the serene temples. The best part was getting to know the locals in Munduk, hearing their stories, their rituals, their values.

There is nothing like traveling to another country to explore, connect with the people and food to make you feel fully alive. The word to describe my entire experience in Munduk — PEACE. I mean look how green it is up in the mountains!! 

I cannot wait to go back. 
Pt.2 of our Bali stay in Nusa Dua is coming soon!

From @jasminestar’s powerful keynote—
✨ Deep wealth = wellness of mind and spirit. Your business (and life) should serve YOU too. 
✨ Your brand is what people say about you when you leave the room. So—what do you want them to say?
✨ Content isn’t just about posting—it’s about connection. Ask questions. Share your why. Tell me how what you do benefits me. Keep it simple & engaging.
✨ A brand is how you make someone FEEL. Make it educating, empowering or entertaining.

✨ 87% of customers look for authenticity in a company. Make your values your guiding principles to be authentic. (@jetsetfarryn of @farrynheight). 

✨ Play long-term games with long-term people. Build for impact, not just quick wins.

✨ Community > audience. An audience says “follow me.” A community says “come with me.” (Thank you, @mrsduley, for this gem.)

✨ You don’t have to do it all. Instead of chasing everything, focus on what actually matters. (Loved @camillestyles’ Sunday journaling method for this!)

✨ Amplify every win. No milestone is too small. (@kathantas)

And my favourite: Apply a new thought to a past experience to change the future outcome. (Also from @jasminestar).   If you want to grow your brand and business (and YOURSELF), get in the room with people you admire and you’ll get there SO much quicker by learning from others that have been in your shoes.

Whether you’re new here or have been here a while...hiiii! 👋🏼 I’m Palak. I wouldn’t be on here if it wasn’t for the connection, so I try and really use this space for exactly that— to connect with you on a deeper level.

1. I’ve been vegetarian my whole life. I’ve only had meat by accident a few times!
2. My name means “moment” — I was actually named by a relative of Gandhi.
3. I once had a food blog called “Not Just Lettuce” highlighting vegetarian dishes at restaurants because that’s all that everyone thought I ate growing up. 😂
4. I used to be an extra for movies and TV. I also did some modelling, and last year I even hand modelled for fun for a commercial haha.

I’ve been in the room with some incredible people, but I’m not phased by fame.
7. I started my own company 8 years ago because I always knew I was meant for more. I knew I’d write a book one day, and I dream of hosting my own show where I interview inspiring people and learn more about their lifestyle. 
8. My husband and I got married in Greece and the local news showed up to our wedding (they hadn’t really seen an Indian and Greek wedding before!).
9. I’ve spent time living in different countries including Canada, Italy, Mexico, Brazil and the US. I’ve traveled to nearly 40 countries and I’m a Canadian and European citizen. I also spend winters away with my husband and dog Bernie, and it’s one of the best decisions I’ve made!
10. I started my membership community, @intheroom.co because I love gathering, connecting and helping people live life in the present moment. When I host events, it’s not because I like event planning but because I love creating spaces for people to be present and expand their lives.

caption:
In today’s “Pinterest perfect, aesthetic everything” world, I know how easy it is to be fearful of inviting people in—worrying that your home isn’t styled perfectly or that your cooking skills aren’t impressive enough. 

But here’s what I believe: welcoming someone into your space is one of the most beautiful acts of connection. 

It’s not about perfection—it’s about presence.

It’s about opening your door and saying, ‘Come as you are, because I want to share this moment with you.’ 

It’s about deepening friendships over shared meals, laughter, and real conversation—not spotless countertops or gourmet dishes.

It’s about allowing the messy to be part of the story. The raw, unfiltered, open, vulnerable parts of YOU.

So if you’ve been holding back, let this be your reminder: the warmth you offer is what makes a home inviting, not how it looks. 

Whether it’s for a cozy chat on the couch, a cup of tea in the afternoon or popcorn and a movie, invite them in anyway and watch how your connections deepen. 🤍
.

Introducing: PEN PALS on SUBSTACK 💌 (formerly The Embiria Edition)

I’ve always loved the timeless tradition of writing letters to a dear friend—thoughtful, personal, and filled with meaning. I remember being in Grade 7 and leaving for the entire summer before school was out, so my bff would write me letters to let me know what happened during the days I missed and which teacher’s class I would be in the next year (and if we’d be together!). Despite being oceans apart, we stayed connected and those letters are something I still cherish.

In a world that moves too fast, that’s exactly what I want this to be. So, I’m renaming my Substack to Pen Pals—a space where I share real reflections, experiences and inspirations to help you slow down, savour real-life moments, and feel more connected to yourself and others amidst our digitally distracted world.

Think of it as a personal note from a friend, filled with what’s been on my mind lately—stories of beautiful living, places and experiences to love, and ways to create more meaningful connections in your life—whether it’s a new café to visit, ideas for hosting or ways to celebrate the everyday moments that matter.

If you crave a little more depth, more joy, and more real in your everyday—this is for you. 

My first letter on “Unlearning Productivity” will be shared soon. 

You might already be subscribed, but if not, head to palakdave.substack.com and join almost 2K others to become a new pen pal. 🫶🏼

caption:
One of the biggest shifts in my life happened when I stopped waiting for ‘someday’ and started creating the reality I truly wanted. ✨

It hit me when the 2nd Winter lockdown during the pandemic was announced. I thought about my well-being, how I’m a social person, how much I missed connection, and how I needed to take care of myself. 

So, my husband and I decided to leave for Tulum, Mexico and spend a few months there.

Was it scary? YES. 
Was it risky? YES. 
Was it out of my comfort zone? YES. 

Was it the best decision I could have made for myself at the time? ABSOLUTELY 100% YES.

Taking that leap allowed me to realize how much more I thrive in an environment that makes me feel like my best self. 

I don’t have to wait until I retire to create MY version of a beautiful life. I could live it in the here and now.

That ONE decision showed me the freedom I could have to spend winters away—trading cold days for sunshine, new adventures, and a pace that feels right for my soul. 

It allowed me to dream up new business ideas, meet new friends, have new experiences, take care of my health and well-being and open up my mind to what’s possible.

This is the 4th year in a row that we’re away for a part of the winter, and it’s still one of the best decisions I’ve ever made because despite everything that’s going on in the world, this is my life and I’m the one that has to create joy for myself so I can show up even better for my community. 🥰

I’ve taken up running outside, I’ve gone kayaking, I’ve swam in natural springs, I get to take Bernie with me to coffee shops, I go for 2 hour walks at sunset and best of all...I’m not spending my days complaining about the weather and wishing things were different (something that I used to do, a LOT).

We get to design the life we want. The question is: what does your best life look like, and what’s stopping you from living it now?
.
.

caption:
Happy 2025!!! 2 weeks later and only a few pictures on my camera roll from the holidays, I’m back from my social media break! 

I think we all know by now that social media doesn’t always leave us feeling so great, but it’s only when we consciously take a step back do we fully FEEL just how good it is to disconnect once in a while.

I spoke to multiple friends who deleted their apps over the holidays and the consensus was loud and clear— EVERYONE felt better. More rested, more refreshed, more present, more connected (which is ironic because these apps were originally designed for connection but have evolved to something totally different). 

If we want to feel those things throughout the year, we can’t ignore the role that social media plays in our day to day lives and how it has an immense impact on us. 

This year, I’m committing to a few things:
🤍 I’m leaning more into my community IRL and @embiriasocialclub off of social media. 
🤍 I’m focusing on my Substack to connect more deeply with all of you.
🤍 I’m speaking at, and attending more in-person events.
🤍 I’m planning and hosting device-free gatherings. 
🤍 I’m logging off the apps on weekends.
🤍 I’m calling my friends more often.
🤍 I’m scheduling a few digital detoxes that are at least a week long.
🤍 And I’m only continuing to share on here from a place of authenticity (which has always been the case). 

I’m not saying this space is all bad…I love the conversations we can have, the messages we can send and the opportunities to connect. But I don’t love the time I waste, the pressure I feel, or how I pick up my phone without even thinking about it. And maybe you feel the same. So, I’m doing a better job of managing my relationship with social media rather than allowing it to manage me.

What’s YOUR intention for 2025 when it comes to your phone usage and social media?
Wishing you more joy, fulfillment and offline memories in your real life for the year ahead! 🥂

caption:
File under: 3rd annual girls weekend — the most wholesome and nourishing few days 🥰
 
For 3 years now, 4 of us friends get together for an immersive weekend of deep chats, belly laughs, and experiences that fill our cup. 

Our first one was at Wander in PEC, then Niagara, and this time I hosted in Toronto!

The weekend was full of: grazing boards, fancy dinners, browsing local shops, cooking meals, playing @werenotreally,  talking at length about human design (we’re all MGs), brainstorming for our businesses, supporting each other’s struggles and cozying up in the living room for about 10 hours of yapping. 😁

If you haven’t spent wholesome quality time like this with your girlfriends in a while— where it’s not about doing, but just being, I highly recommend. The best way to describe it is SOUL NOURISHING. 

When we were shopping at KOTN, one of the girls working there asked what we were up to, so we told her about our annual weekend to which she responded “that is the sweetest thing ever— you’re making me want to call my girlfriends right after work to plan something exactly like this”. 🥹

And that’s more than I could ask for— inspiring you to live a life surrounded by genuine connections and fulfilling experiences just like this. 

That’s exactly what I hope for you. The experiences you’ll remember for years to come, with the people you love spending time with. 

Grateful to these girls @christine.duross @iamlauraabate and especially @artijalan for bringing us together! 3 years ago not all of us had even met, and now this tradition is something I look forward to each year. 🤍

The New Truth Podcast - Season 2 - Episode 48: Reclaim Your Life from Digital Overload with Palak Dave

In this episode, Catherine & I interview Palak Dave - a champion of intentional living and founder of Embiria Social Club. Palak shares the secrets about how to escape the noise of social media, and learn the art of making connections in real life.  She reveals the extensive impact of technology overload - and how to motivate yourself to make the changes needed for a more present, fulfilling and truly connected life.  

About Palak Dave:

@paldave is a mission-driven entrepreneur, experience expert, speaker and author of Beautiful Everydays: A Guide to Living in the Here and Now. A former award-winning marketer with senior roles at Toronto International Film Festival and Indigo Books and Music, Palak founded Embiria in 2017, which has since evolved to Embiria Social Club (ESC), a community helping women feel more fulfilled in their everyday lives. She has curated over 350 events, partnering with global brands like Lululemon and Bumble. Palak is passionate about championing a movement towards everyday fulfillment and real-life connections over digital distractions. She has traveled to nearly 40 countries and currently resides in Toronto, Canada.

ARE YOU HOSTING FOR THE HOLIDAYS? SAVE THIS POST FOR HOW TO A BUILD AN EASY GIANT CHARCUTERIE BOARD THAT WILL IMPRESS YOUR GUESTS.🎄✨

Hosting can feel intimidating, but I promise it doesn’t have to be hard. You don’t have to cook a 5 course meal or even worry about keeping everything warm. 

Instead of a full dinner for our holiday drop-in party, I decided to create a giant board instead.  I picked up a bunch of pizzas and cut them into tiny squares served alongside garlic bread as the main part of the board to build around so that it’s still filling, but fun!

Add some crackers, cheese, fruit, nuts, desserts and voilà!! You have yourself a board that wows your guests. 

TIP: save a bit of room on the board to add any last minute items that guests bring such as cookies, chocolates etc. 

The more, the merrier. 

Let me know if you try this idea out over the holidays! 

HAPPY HOSTING! 🥂

caption:
At the start of 2024, I set a clear intention: to share my mission and message through more speaking engagements. 

I thrive on deep, meaningful conversations, so stepping into spaces that aligned with my passions felt like the natural next step. 

I set ambitious goals—10 podcast interviews, panels and events that resonated with me, and collaborations with brands I admire. And because I claimed that energy, the universe responded in ways beyond what I imagined.

Here’s what unfolded: 🎙️ 40+ podcast interviews, including @asianbossgirl and @theknowwithnikkispo  🎤 Moderated and participated in 5 panels on topics close to my heart 🗝️ Delivered my first keynote, sharing a deeply personal experience that shaped the work I do today. It was nerve-wracking and emotional, but hearing from women afterward about how my story impacted them made it all worth it. 📰 Featured in publications I admire, including @theeverygirl, to share my expertise and perspective 🤝 Hosted and co-hosted live shows and events for incredible brands like @threeshipsbeauty and @wildehousepaper 

This year taught me something important: when we truly lean into our dreams and claim them, we open the door to incredible possibilities. I’ve also learned to quiet my inner “imposter syndrome” (well, mostly 😆) and embrace that I do have something valuable to share.

So here’s my message to you: if there’s a little voice in the back of your mind urging you toward something, listen to it. Lean in. Claim it. It’s there for a reason, and you’re capable of making it happen—maybe even bigger and better than you imagined.

Looking ahead to 2025, I’m dreaming even bigger: ✨ More paid speaking engagements ✨ More incredible podcast interviews (starting tomorrow with @staci.millard) ✨ Panels and events that inspire connection and impact

Here’s where you’ll see me next: 1️⃣ Ripple Effects Panel by @danikreeftwrites: Talking about building communities with @workwomb, @amandalchase (only $22 to join—link in Stories!) 2️⃣ @highvibe.women Panel in March: Sharing insights on the power of connection

And I’m just getting started! What’s on your dream list for 2025? CLAIM IT!

caption:
Last night I celebrated my 40th birthday in my favourite way—an intimate dinner party with great food, great friends and meaningful conversations. 

The theme was La Dolce Vita, all about celebrating life’s pleasures, and of course my love of all things Italian. 🍷🍝 

10 years ago I set out to create more community in my life. It’s one of the reasons I started a company centered around shared experiences, so that I could personally feel more connected. 

It’s wild to say, but only now, 10 whole years later do I fully feel that without a doubt I have the most incredible community of people around me. I have spent the past decade actively working on cultivate deeper relationships…I reach out, I make plans, I show up…(I even pick up the phone when it rings! lol) and in return, my community (both near and far) does the same for me. 

That wouldn’t have happened without putting in the effort. And I’m here to tell you, when you do, it is the most rewarding feeling. It’s also why I created @embiriasocialclub, so you can experience that sense of the community you might be craving. 

Last night, my husband asked everyone to go around the table and share something they appreciated about me. I was moved to tears with the countless memories I’ve been able to make with everyone, with the laughs we’ve shared, the experiences we’ve had and all that is still to come. 

I truly felt so loved and I’m so grateful to everyone that made last night one of the most magical nights of my life. 🥰 THANK YOU! If this is what 40 feels like, I’ll take it. 

A very special thanks to Ayah of @oui_aia for cooking the most delicious 5 course meal! It was perfection. 

All this to say — go and celebrate life’s moments. The big ones and the small. Host a party. Make memories! Live la dolce vita! 

My sister said I’ve apparently been planning my own birthday parties since I was 4 years old…so I guess that means I’m exactly where I was always meant to be. 🥹

caption:
Couldn’t have said this better myself. 

Yes, tech can be used for good — like getting to FaceTime someone across the world, or listening to a podcast you love while in the car…

BUT how many times have you been on your phone for wayyyy longer than intended, realizing you’re doing something completely different than what wanted to when you initially reached for it?? 

Digital wellness habits are something you have to build for yourself. When you realize that your phone has a bit more control over you than you’d like — it’s time for you to take control of your time back.

Less phone time = more presence. 

That can mean more nights connecting with your partner instead of scrolling in bed. 

More walks noticing the gorgeous fall colours.

More presence when you’re around your parents or kids. 

More time for a new hobby. 

And ultimately, more peace of mind. 

For more of my insights on the topic of digital wellness habits, you can check out any of my latest podcast interviews (link is in my profile). 

I hope you enjoy some offline time this weekend! 
(And if you do, notice how good it makes you feel).

caption:
5 months of experiences with extraordinary women who share the desire to connect authentically, grow deeply and find fulfillment in their everyday regardless of how busy life can feel. That’s @embiriasocialclub.

When I started curating events 7 years ago, my goal was simple—it was to bring women together to find the sense of community and belonging that they always wished they had.

I quickly realized that it really didn’t matter what activity they were doing, sharing an experience together was enough to make them leave feeling more fulfilled than when they came.

I kept imaging ways they could connect outside of the events I hosted. Through group chats, more event series, following one another on IG. 
But I wanted it to go deeper, and so did they.

Fast forward 7 years, and almost 500 events later, these women now have a space to call their own (both online and off).

Embiria Social Club was created for them—and for you—the women craving more meaningful friendships, the women who have big dreams but shouldn’t have to feel alone, the women who cheer each other on, the women who have insights to share, the women who love a beautiful experience to chat about life and enjoy a great meal together. 

It’s only been 5 months of ESC, and we’ve already shared dozens of experiences together through coffee dates, connection calls, beautiful dinners, wellness classes, manifestation workshops & even a private @soulchocolate tasting.

AND WE’RE JUST GETTING STARTED!!!

Our online hub is where members come together to chat, offer recommendations, send DMs, make plans & RSVP to events. They also enjoy monthly giveaways, perks from our fave brands (like @wildehousepaper, @op_e___n, @stellar.eats, @threeshipsbeauty) and then we move the connection offline for IRL events & gatherings that deepen our relationships with one another & ourselves. 

ESC is more than a community—in today’s digitally driven world it’s a movement for women seeking real-life connections & experiences to feel more fulfilled. 

There’s so much in store for 2025 so if any of this resonates, I invite you to listen to your intuition & join us for less than the cost of a monthly brunch.

caption:
I spoke on a panel at an event for women entrepreneurs and thought leaders yesterday, and someone from the audience asked me “what does success look like to you?”. 

My answer was that success to me means FREEDOM and FULFILLMENT.

THE FREEDOM TO do what I want with my time, create my own schedule, tune into my needs and plan things accordingly. 

Freedom to say YES to things that feel aligned, and no thank you to things that don’t. Freedom to spend time with the people I care about, and to take care of my well-being first.

And because of this freedom, I feel fulfilled. I get to create a life I love, do work that lights me up, build dream partnerships, work with people that inspire me and have experiences that bring me joy. I get to purse my passions, and despite the challenges and ups and downs of entrepreneurship, I continue to check in to make sure that I’m following what feels fulfilling.

If you’re an entrepreneur, you can probably relate to the fact that having freedom and fulfillment is a key factor to why you continue to do what you do. These things can result in you feeling successful in your business, because you’re making sure that your cup feels full. And from that place, the abundance will flow...

If you haven’t thought about this question in a while, then take a second to reflect on what success looks like for you? 

What words come to mind? 
Where do you find fulfillment in your day to day? 
I’d love to hear what you value most when you think of success…and are you living it in the here and now? 
.
.
.

caption:
A few weekends ago I hosted an beautiful morning of connection with an in-person community event for @sreal.ca real estate to support the opening of a new local café @thegreenwood_cafe while inviting neighbours to mingle over a free coffee or latte, courtesy of @sreal.ca. ☕️ 

For 7 years now I’ve hosted and co-hosted and curated hundreds of IRL events — for brands, media, influencers and local businesses and the one thing I know for sure is NOTHING beats the feeling of connecting in-person. 

It’s your smile when you hold the door open for someone. 
A handshake to you introduce yourself.
Handing a beverage over as a kind gesture. 
Waving to a baby. 
Petting someone’s dog. 
Having conversations out of curiosity and connecting over commonalities that you overhear like the same coffee order, or your favourite local bookstore. 
A warm hug to say goodbye. 

All of these things cannot happen over a screen. 

All of these things are what make us human, what help us connect with eachother and the world around us, and allow us to feel fulfilled. 

My favourite thing is having experiences like this in the real world that help us connect and realize that we’re never alone. 

If you’re a brand that’s wanting to spread awareness and build more of a community, host something IN PERSON (and send me a msg if you want support in hosting and fostering genuine connections amongst your customers). 

You don’t need a huge budget, it can be as simple as a coffee meet up or a community walk. 

In a world where everyone is digitally overwhelmed, move the connection from online to offline and watch the magic unfold. ✨
.
.
.
.
.

caption:
Celebrating 40 today.🎈

I’ve never been one to care about my age, but 40 feels different. It feels more significant, and more “adult”, even though I know I’ve been an adult for years now. But this feels like being a *real* adult. 

In my mind I still feel 29. They say that happens…that you sort of stay at an age where you hold a lot of memories. 

I think there’s a lot that 40 holds, too. It could be because it’s a “midpoint” in life. Or because I relate less and less to the younger generation. Or that I need to go to chiro to feel good in my body, I don’t love driving at nights as much and when I’m getting up after sitting cross legged for a while I’m vocal about the effort it takes.😅 

There’s a lot that I wanted to accomplish by 40. And although I constantly have people telling me I’ve done SO much — I still feel like I’m just getting started. 

My 30s were a beautiful decade. I got married, started my own company, moved to two different homes, got a puppy, hosted thousands of women at hundreds of events I curated, became an Airbnb host, made it through a pandemic with many business pivots along the way, spent winters away for 4 years in a row, wrote and published a book, launched a membership community that I believe is truly making an impact and traveled to my 40th country recently (coincidentally!). 

And YET, I feel certain that this decade will bring so much more. @verawang started her company at 40, and that really resonated with me. It makes me hopeful for what’s ahead and that I can dream big because anything is possible. I also know that we’ll all never be as young as we are today — so we have to cherish it!

I’m grateful for the all of the years of life I have had the privilege of experiencing, for all of you that have been a part of the journey so far and the love that I feel surrounded by, today and everyday. Thank you for all of the wishes. 🥰

Cheers to a new decade…I’m looking forward to all that is to come!🥂
